title: Short Stuff: Cleveland’s Infamous 10-Cent Beer Night
summary: Short Stuff episode on Cleveland's infamous 10-Cent Beer Night, a June 4, 1974 Cleveland Indians home game against the Texas Rangers. The hosts cover the promotion's background and inflation-adjusted price, the previous week's brawl at the Rangers' Arlington stadium with Billy Martin's remark about Cleveland's small crowds, sports talk host Pete Franklin riling up fans, and the game itself: overwhelmed beer vendors, streakers, fireworks thrown at the Rangers' dugout, and the Jeff Burrows hat incident that set off a field riot in which the Rangers and Indians players fought fans. Umpire Nestor Chylak was injured, the game was forfeited to Texas, and the Indians then limited future beer nights to four beers per person.

segments.title: Introduction to Cleveland's 10-Cent Beer Night
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the Cleveland history topic and note the ten-cent beer promotion was routine across baseball, worth about 57 cents today.

segments.title: Background: the Rangers brawl and Billy Martin's remark
segments.summary: The hosts describe the prior week's ten-cent beer night in Arlington, where a brawl broke out after a hard slide and retaliation. Billy Martin, coaching Texas, said he was not worried about Cleveland's fans in retaliation because they did not have enough fans.

segments.title: Pete Franklin riles up Cleveland
segments.summary: Sports talk radio host Pete Franklin spent much of his show stirring up Cleveland fans against the Rangers in the week before the game.

segments.title: Mid-episode break
segments.summary: Hosts take a break before describing the game, which they note was actually on June 4 rather than June 6.

segments.title: Crowd, beer vendors and streakers
segments.summary: About 20,000 fans attended. Vendors were overwhelmed by beer demand, trucks were pulled near the outfield, and two teenage girls at a beer stand fled. Streakers ran onto the field during the game, including a father and son who mooned the bleachers.

segments.title: Hit-by-pitch, fireworks and the field riot
segments.summary: After Ferguson Jenkins was hit by a line drive from Leron Lee, fans chanted for more hits and threw objects while Billy Martin blew kisses at the crowd. Fans fired fireworks into the Rangers' dugout. When Jeff Burrows was tackled by a fan trying to grab his hat, Texas players charged the field with bats, met by fans carrying knives, chains and torn-up seats. Umpire Nestor Chylak was injured and the game was forfeited to Texas.

segments.title: Aftermath and beer limits
segments.summary: The Indians kept three more scheduled beer nights but limited sales to four beers per person instead of unlimited. Reported figures include about 60,000 beers consumed, 19 streakers, and stolen bases never recovered.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts reflect on the chaos, invite listener stories, and close the episode.
